neighbours.label: Light skin or hair as a trait of a person or group (fair skin, fair-haired, blonde, poor whites); the same words for other things stay quiet
fire: Sunscreen matters most for those with fair skin and freckles.
Her sister was a fair-haired girl with pale eyes.
Vikings are often pictured as tall and blond in old films.
The novel follows poor white farmers in the Georgia hills.
Marriage notices in the paper asked for a fair bride.
He remembered a blonde child playing near the gate.
In that census, white settlers outnumbered everyone else.
Redheads and other pale people burn quickly in the sun.
quiet: Sunscreen matters most for those on long hikes and boats.
Her sister was a curly-haired girl with sharp eyes.
Vikings are often pictured as loud and rude in old films.
The novel follows poor tenant farmers in the Georgia hills.
Marriage notices in the paper appeared on Sunday.
He remembered a white fence standing near the gate.
In that census, sheep farmers outnumbered everyone else.
The county fair and other summer events drew crowds in the sun.

short: fair skin, blond, white as trait
notes: The other pole reads minority, black, color line, so the unit looks like complexion or race.
